speaker: CREW_DIGGER
lines: Pulled an ironwood pile out of the bottom silt. Incisor marks all over the butt end.
Not your teeth, FOREMAN. That timber was felled over a century ago and cured in salt.
Whoever built the first wall here knew how to notch a sill.
clue: Beavers were hired to dam this exact gorge long before FOREMAN arrived.

speaker: CREW_WATCHER
lines: Listen to the backwash when the surge drops off row zero.
Open water doesn't echo on a seventy-five-second beat like that. A basin does.
The water isn't pushing the wall, boss. It's pacing the room.
clue: The tide's rhythm behaves like water resonating inside an enclosed basin, not an open coast.

speaker: FOREMAN
lines: An oiled linen survey chart rolled inside a brass tube. The eastern margin has been sheared off with scissors.
If you lay the valley orchard contours against the outer headland, the elevation lines lock together.
The thirty-foot contour in the village is the old high-water mark.
clue: The valley's topography matches the outer coastline; someone trimmed the official map to hide it.

speaker: CREW_MASON
lines: Slate tally board wedged under a ruin course. Four hundred clean tides scratched in neat rows of five.
Stops halfway through a fifth stroke. Chisel's still sitting beside it, wrapped in oiled rag.
The wall didn't break on them. They just stopped counting.
clue: An earlier foreman did not fail or drown; they deliberately walked off the job mid-tide.
